claim: The DDoS resiliency whitepaper says AWS edge locations add a layer of network infrastructure that helps optimize latency and throughput, absorb DDoS attacks and isolate faults for any application that uses Amazon CloudFront, Global Accelerator and Amazon Route 53.
question: Which AWS services give an application the edge-location benefits for absorbing DDoS attacks?

values.display: Amazon CloudFront, Global Accelerator and Amazon Route 53

qualifiers.scope: AWS Best Practices for DDoS Resiliency, BP1 and BP3

evidence.quote: Access to highly scaled, diverse internet connections can significantly increase your ability to optimize latency and throughput to users, to absorb DDoS attacks, and to isolate faults while minimizing the impact on your application's availability. AWS edge locations provide an additional layer of network infrastructure that provides these benefits to any application that uses Amazon CloudFront, Global Accelerator and Amazon Route 53.

claim: With Global Accelerator you put its two static IPv4 addresses (or two IPv4 and two IPv6 addresses for dual-stack) on allow lists just once, in client applications, firewalls and DNS records, and you can add or remove endpoints in Regions, run blue/green deployments and do A/B testing without updating those addresses.
question: Why is Global Accelerator useful when clients cannot be updated often?

values.display: include these addresses on allow lists just once
run blue/green deployment, and do A/B testing

evidence.quote: You include these addresses on allow lists just once in your client applications, firewalls, and DNS records. With Global Accelerator, you can add or remove endpoints in AWS Regions, run blue/green deployment, and do A/B testing without having to update the IP addresses in your client applications.
It lets you associate regional resources, such as load balancers and Amazon EC2 instances, to two static IPv4 addresses or, for dual-stack, to two static IPv4 addresses and two IPv6 addresses.

claim: You can configure the traffic dial together with endpoint weights to set up load sharing between application endpoints, including active-active and active-standby multi-Region architectures.
question: Which Global Accelerator features let you build active-active or active-standby multi-Region setups?

evidence.quote: You can configure the traffic dial and endpoint weights to implement complex scenarios as well, to configure load sharing between application endpoints. With these Global Accelerator features, you can deploy and run applications in multi-Region architectures, including active-active and active-standby setups.

note: d137 (Callvale stage 4: us-east-1 active, us-west-2 standby).

claim: When OAC secures an Amazon S3 origin, communication between CloudFront and Amazon S3 always uses HTTPS, but only when you choose to always sign requests.
question: When is the CloudFront to S3 connection always HTTPS with origin access control?

values.display: only when you choose to always sign requests

qualifiers.scope: CloudFront origin access control for Amazon S3
qualifiers.condition: the signing behavior is set to always sign requests

evidence.quote: When you use OAC to secure your Amazon S3 origin, communication between CloudFront and Amazon S3 is always through HTTPS, but only when you choose to always sign requests.

claim: When you use CloudFront OAC with Amazon S3 bucket origins, you must set Amazon S3 Object Ownership to Bucket owner enforced, which is the default for new buckets.
question: Which S3 Object Ownership setting does OAC require?

values.display: the default for new Amazon S3 buckets

qualifiers.scope: CloudFront OAC with Amazon S3 bucket origins
qualifiers.condition: if ACLs are required, the Bucket owner preferred setting is the alternative

evidence.quote: When you use CloudFront OAC with Amazon S3 bucket origins, you must set Amazon S3 Object Ownership to Bucket owner enforced, the default for new Amazon S3 buckets. If you require ACLs, use the Bucket owner preferred setting to maintain control over objects uploaded by using CloudFront.

claim: OAC does not support origin redirect by using Lambda@Edge.
question: Can an origin redirect done with Lambda@Edge be combined with OAC?

values.display: OAC doesn't support origin redirect by using Lambda@Edge

qualifiers.scope: CloudFront OAC for Amazon S3 origins

evidence.quote: OAC doesn't support origin redirect by using Lambda@Edge.

claim: When an Application Load Balancer is the origin, you can configure CloudFront to prevent users from directly accessing the Application Load Balancer, so that users reach it only through CloudFront.
question: How do you make sure users reach an ALB origin only through CloudFront?

values.display: configure CloudFront to prevent users from directly accessing the Application Load Balancer
access the Application Load Balancer only through CloudFront

qualifiers.scope: CloudFront with an Application Load Balancer origin

evidence.quote: When you use CloudFront with an Application Load Balancer in Elastic Load Balancing as the origin, you can configure CloudFront to prevent users from directly accessing the Application Load Balancer. This allows users to access the Application Load Balancer only through CloudFront, making sure that you get the benefits of using CloudFront.

claim: To encrypt data in transit with CloudFront you configure it to require HTTPS from viewers, and you can also configure it to use HTTPS to get files from your origin.
question: How do you encrypt both legs of a CloudFront connection in transit?

values.display: require that viewers use HTTPS to request your files
use HTTPS to get files from your origin

evidence.quote: To encrypt your data during transit, you configure Amazon CloudFront to require that viewers use HTTPS to request your files, so that connections are encrypted when CloudFront communicates with viewers. You also can configure CloudFront to use HTTPS to get files from your origin, so that connections are encrypted when CloudFront communicates with your origin.

claim: CloudFront Functions code and configuration is always stored in an encrypted format on the edge location POPs and in other storage locations used by CloudFront, and it is always encrypted in transit when copied to the POPs.
question: Is CloudFront Functions code encrypted at rest and in transit?

values.display: always stored in an encrypted format

evidence.quote: Function code and configuration in CloudFront Functions is always encrypted in transit when copied to the edge location points of presence (POPs), and between other storage locations used by CloudFront.
Function code and configuration in CloudFront Functions is always stored in an encrypted format on the edge location POPs, and in other storage locations used by CloudFront.
